title: Race starts on the ground and finishes like the original — host checkpoint
summary: Race grids no longer hang in the air through the countdown, and a finished race now ends the way the original does: results with estimated CPU times while every racer keeps driving. PR #112 (commit d1ad2f5) is implementation-ready and auto-merging; this is a host checkpoint, not a verified public release.
details: Start: ATVs are placed with the original grid placement routine (001dd440): heading kept horizontal, roll matched to the terrain normal, then lifted by the deepest wheel penetration. Physics now runs during the countdown with everyone braking, so the grid no longer floats about 2.5 ft up. Race resets use the same placement.

Finish: the race-over flow follows the original RaceStatus (00248b20). The game does not wait for CPUs; unfinished CPUs receive the original estimated total, last and best lap times derived from their gap to the leader's pace, with an increasing-order tie-break. Nobody freezes at the finish: all racers keep driving and the player's ATV or motorcycle is handed to the recovered CPU path driver. The Race Results menu mirrors the original (rider, total time, best lap); Continue leads to Restart / Quit Event, and Hide Menu / Show Results lets the player watch the field.

Discoveries: the original pre-race intro camera shots (<venue>nat1/2.vub) and a per-course TV camera director (<venue>nat.tv, 13 to 25 cameras) exist in the disc data and are the next step. No whole-race replay feature exists in ATV2; only Lap Attack ghosts and a STOPCAM cheat.

Verification (host): Rust tests and Clippy pass; the content browser tests test_race.mjs and test_race_courses.mjs (all 32 courses) pass. A host 1-lap SX01 race finished with estimated CPU times and continued CPU-driven driving at about 75 mph. Screenshots are host captures: grid on the ground during the countdown, the results table with estimated CPU times, and the menu hidden with the CPU-driven player continuing.
limitation: Host-only; PR #112 is not yet publicly verified. The takeover routine that hands the player to the CPU driver is not identified in the exact-build code, so it follows the original's observed presentation. Stunt Score and Profile Points result columns are omitted. The original estimate gives a very short best lap to CPUs that never completed a lap (for example in 1-lap races); this is kept as original. Motorcycle resets keep an authored 2.5 ft drop. Intro cameras and the TV camera director are not implemented yet.
caption: Host SX01 capture: Race Results after a 1-lap race, with estimated CPU total times and best laps; the other host captures (grid on the ground in the countdown, CPU-driven player after the finish) are recorded in the verification notes.
